text: If all the ice on Earth melted, the sea would rise about seventy meters. That's a twenty-storey building.
Almost all of that ice sits in two places. Antarctica holds about ninety-one percent. Greenland, about eight.
Every mountain glacier on the planet? Just one percent.
Melt it, and the sea comes up the beach, over the boardwalk, and into town.
First floor, gone. Fifth floor, gone. By the tenth floor, the fish are window shopping.
Low countries vanish, and every coastline on the map gets redrawn.
But here's the twist. The ice floating at the North Pole? Melt all of it, and the sea barely moves.
Floating ice already pushes aside its own weight in water, just like an ice cube melting in a glass.
It's the ice sitting on land that does the damage.
Luckily, melting all of it would take thousands of years. Unluckily, the sea is already rising.
So maybe skip the beach house, and buy the one on the hill.
